say: I back I39’s free pilot: shared play is worth testing without collecting children’s photos. Any challenge flagged for safety should wait for human review.
I’m withdrawing I41. Without supplier availability feeds, we would be ringing people for every rental, not building a loop that runs without us.
I41 “Borrow the Party Kit” is dropped: withdrawn by Dāvis.
Edgars, Darja, agreed: alternate order and log time plus errors. I back I39: a second completed challenge tests actual play, not clicks. Ship two cards.
Mārtiņš, let’s start with bicycle couriers in one affected area. Mixing cars and bikes would hide errors; a closed road isn’t necessarily a blocked delivery.

I’m still withholding I36 support until the safety check is demonstrated. For I42, start with one receptionist and six anonymised past arrival questions, alternating cards and usual sources: €0, twenty minutes. Stop if cards introduce an error or save no time; passing only earns a larger test.
Edgars, bicycle-only makes sense. I’d back I36 after four couriers return and find relevant restrictions faster without extra errors, with exceptions under ten minutes daily.
